attrs.ifname_escape: Replace '-' with '_' and percent-escape any non-[A-Za-z0-9_] as _XX (lowercase hex). Example: wlan-foo -> wlan_foo, eth0:1 -> eth0_3a1.
attrs.rename_behavior: A kernel rename (RTM_NEWLINK with same ifindex but new IFLA_IFNAME — typically systemd's predictable-name renamer at boot, or 'ip link set name …') surfaces as InterfacesRemoved on the old path followed by InterfacesAdded on the new path. The interface keeps the same Ifindex but every cached property is re-read at the new path. Subscribers should track interfaces by ObjectManager events rather than caching the path string.

attrs.bssid_format: 12 lowercase hex chars, no separators (e.g. aabbccddeeff)
attrs.lifecycle: Transient. Subscribe via ObjectManager InterfacesAdded/Removed; do not poll.

attrs.device_address_format: BlueZ-style with colons replaced by underscores, e.g. AA_BB_CC_DD_EE_FF
attrs.note: Path uses adapter ifindex segment, not ifname; matches BlueZ object layout.

attrs.status: reserved; appears once DD-004 ships persistence

attrs.note: Canonical source of truth for the current object set. Convenience properties (Manager.WifiProfiles, Wifi.ScanResults) may lag during concurrent modifications.

attrs.ownership: external — systemd-networkd, NOT nexusd. Lives on the same system bus.
attrs.purpose: Layer-3 source of truth: IPv4 / IPv6 addresses, routes, DHCP lease, etc. nexusd delegates IP management here per nexus-architecture.md ADR-001 (`No built-in IP management`). Clients that need IP rows on a connected card read them from this service, not from fi.nexus1.
attrs.key_method: DescribeLink(ifindex:i) -> (json:s) — per-link JSON dump with Addresses[], Routes[], DHCPv4{}, DHCPv6{}. networkctl status parses the same shape. (Older systemds (<250) only expose the no-arg `Describe() -> (json:s)` manager-wide dump; in that case extract the per-link blob from JSON.Interfaces[] by Index.)
attrs.fallback_method: Describe() -> (json:s) — manager-wide JSON dump. Returned blob has `Interfaces` (array of per-link objects, each with `Index`, `Addresses`, `Routes`, …). Use as a fallback on systemd <250.

attrs.path_escape: ifindex is rendered as `_<n>` (underscore + decimal int). Resolve via Interface.Ifindex on the matching fi.nexus1 interface.
key_properties_for_ui: OperationalState (s) — 'off' | 'no-carrier' | 'dormant' | 'degraded' | 'enslaved' | 'carrier' | 'degraded-carrier' | 'routable' | 'enslaved-routable' (becomes 'routable' once IPv4/IPv6 routing is up)
IPv4AddressState (s) / IPv6AddressState (s) — same enum as AddressState but per family
attrs.subscription_pattern: PropertiesChanged on this object is the trigger to re-call org.freedesktop.network1.Manager.DescribeLink(ifindex) and refresh the rendered Address / Route rows. The Link interface itself does NOT expose Addresses[] / Routes[] as bus properties — DescribeLink() (or, on systemd <250, the manager-wide Describe()) is the authoritative source.

key_properties_for_ui: DNS (a(iay)) — array of (family:i, address:ay). family=2 (AF_INET) for IPv4, family=10 (AF_INET6) for IPv6.
DNSSEC (s), DNSOverTLS (s) — capability strings; render only if the UI surfaces secure-DNS state.
attrs.subscription_pattern: PropertiesChanged on this object fires when DNS configuration changes. Reliable for DNS-row updates without re-resolving the whole IP block.

attrs.note: Monotonic feature-detection tokens. Additive within an API major version.

attrs.purpose: Last observed internet-reachability state from the daemon's connectivity probe (HTTP/1.1 GET against http://connectivity-check.ubuntu.com/ by default). `internetUnknown` is the pre-probe initial value; on nexusd startup the daemon runs one probe and emits the result, so consumers should not see Unknown after the first event-loop tick. The state is purely event-driven: a probe runs on every Wi-Fi / Ethernet `LinkReady`, and the state flips to `internetOffline` immediately when the last `LinkLost` drops the set to empty (no probe wait). There is no periodic backstop — between link transitions the state is sticky.
attrs.subscription_pattern: Subscribe to sig:fi.nexus.Manager.InternetConnectivityChanged (preferred) or watch PropertiesChanged on /fi/nexus1; the property mirrors the signal so a polling client only needs the property.
attrs.note: Captive-portal detection is HTTP-only by design — an HTTPS probe would have to MITM TLS to detect a portal, and the failure mode is indistinguishable from offline. Plain HTTP exposes the portal explicitly via a 200/3xx response instead of the canonical 204. Tradeoff of the no-backstop design: a portal session expiring or an ISP outage that doesn't drop carrier will go undetected until the next link transition; consumers that need stricter freshness should run their own application-layer probe.
ay (not s) handles non-UTF-8 SSIDs.

attrs.credentials: Cleartext on the wire; encrypted on disk by Profile Store.
attrs.uniqueness: At most one profile per SSID. Repeat -> AlreadyExists; use Profile.Update.
At most one profile per ifname.

attrs.purpose: Forget a stored profile. Removes it from the in-memory cache and the on-disk profile store; the backend will not auto-connect to it again. Path may point to either a wifi profile (/fi/nexus1/profile/wifi/<ulid>) or an ethernet profile (/fi/nexus1/profile/ethernet/<ulid>).
attrs.side_effect: Disconnects any active connection using this profile.

attrs.exclusivity: At most one outstanding lease at a time

attrs.note: Releasing an already-expired lease returns NotFound; safe for unconditional cleanup paths.

attrs.transport: Unix file descriptor (avoids D-Bus message-size limits). Read until EOF.
attrs.size_hint: 10-100 KB typical; up to several MB with verbose logs

attrs.note: Operator-facing notifications that don't fit a specific interface. Treat unknown kinds as displayable key/value.

attrs.fires_on: Transition only — not on every probe. Pure event-driven state machine: probe on `WifiLinkReady`/`EthLinkReady` (immediate); on `WifiLinkLost`/`EthLinkLost` for the last link, publish `internetOffline` immediately without probing. nexusd also emits one probe-driven transition at startup so the initial state isn't Unknown. There is no periodic backstop.

attrs.note: All property updates flow through here. Hot props are coalesced (~1Hz); cold props are immediate.

attrs.remediation: Profile.Update with new credential field; backend clears CredentialsInvalid and retries on next auto-connect cycle.

attrs.fires_on: DD-002 §9.3 fail-fast 802.1X failure (BadCredentials, CertificateRejected). Retriable failures stay silent and just go through Interface.StateChanged.
attrs.remediation: Update the per-interface profile (Profile.Ethernet.Update with new client_cert/private_key/password). Profile-store credentials_invalid flag for ethernet is not yet wired (EthernetProfile schema lacks the field); this notification is the only operator-facing surface today.

attrs.note: Reserved kind; not currently emitted. Ethernet uses the lifecycle path instead — when wpa_supplicant disappears, every in-flight Authenticating/Authenticated interface drops to auth_failed via Interface.StateChanged with details.reason='server_unreachable', and EthLinkLost tears IP down via systemd-networkd.

Empty for GNSS. For a Bluetooth adapter, may read as all-zero right after the adapter first appears — either briefly (firmware on some BCM/Cypress/Marvell parts sets the real BD_ADDR after kernel registration) or indefinitely on UART/serdev-attached controllers, which never expose a kernel sysfs address at all. Nexus self-corrects it from BlueZ's own Adapter1.Address (polled once per second while connected) in both cases, with no PropertiesChanged signal on this property today, so a zeroed value seen immediately after discovery is worth a re-Get a second or two later rather than treated as a permanent fault.

details_keys.profile: o (any technology, when a stored profile drove the transition)
details_keys.eap_method: s (Ethernet Authenticating; matches Ethernet.EapMethod values e.g. PEAP, TLS)

attrs.note: Object path of the emitting interface identifies which device. Match by interface+member, filter by path. Ethernet fires this on every EthInterfaceState transition (waiting_carrier ↔ link_ready, authenticating ↔ authenticated ↔ auth_failed).
attrs.transition_only: Idempotent since nexus-dbus 0.13.2: a re-emission with the same (state, details) tuple is suppressed daemon-side. Consumers do not need to dedup on their side.
attrs.consistency: When this signal fires for a Wi-Fi interface with state='connected', the daemon flushes pending PropertiesChanged for prop:fi.nexus.Interface.OperState, prop:fi.nexus.Interface.Carrier, and prop:fi.nexus.Wifi.Powered before the StateChanged signal lands. A consumer that reads those properties immediately on the connected edge sees Up / true / true rather than the pre-connect values.

attrs.consistency_with_powered: Since nexus-dbus 0.14.0, prop:fi.nexus.Wifi.Powered=false implies State ∈ {disconnected, idle}: the dbus event loop synthesizes a State='disconnected' (with `details.reason='rf_killed'` on the StateChanged edge) on every Powered=false transition, regardless of whether the wifi backend has separately emitted a Disconnected event. Since nexus-wifi 0.17.0, the wifi backend ALSO drives its own state machine to Disconnected{RfKilled} on every rfkill engage (both the kernel `/dev/rfkill` watcher path and the operator `SetPowered=false` path), so the synthesized signal and the backend-driven signal carry identical fingerprints and the second is deduped. The result: a late-arriving wpa_supplicant `Disconnected{LocalRequest|other}` no longer overwrites the `rf_killed` reason. Conversely, a bare Powered=false→true with no Connect call does NOT carry the prior `connected`/`roaming`/etc. value forward — State stays `disconnected` until the wifi backend folds RfKilled to `idle` and the auto-select path kicks a fresh scan.

attrs.sentinel: All zero/empty when not connected; check Wifi.State, do not infer.

attrs.lifecycle: Since nexus-dbus 0.14.0, the daemon DROPS the cached scan-result set on every prop:fi.nexus.Wifi.Powered=false transition — the array empties, the underlying `fi.nexus.ScanResult` per-BSSID objects are removed from the object tree (org.freedesktop.DBus.ObjectManager.InterfacesRemoved fires for each), and a power-on cycle starts with an empty cache that the next sig:fi.nexus.Wifi.ScanComplete repopulates. Consumers can no longer observe a stale path list with `Powered=false`. (Earlier builds retained the array; that was a stale-data trap.)

attrs.note: rfkill release for this interface
attrs.consistency_with_state: Bidirectional invariant. (1) Since nexus-dbus 0.13.2, when prop:fi.nexus.Wifi.State (or sig:fi.nexus.Wifi.StateChanged) shows a connected interface, this property is guaranteed to read `true` — the daemon flushes the pending PropertiesChanged for `Powered` before the StateChanged edge fires. Same guarantee holds for prop:fi.nexus.Interface.OperState (Up) and prop:fi.nexus.Interface.Carrier (true). (2) Since nexus-dbus 0.14.0, when this property transitions to `false` (rfkill engaged or operator write), the daemon synchronously lands prop:fi.nexus.Wifi.State='disconnected', clears prop:fi.nexus.Wifi.ConnectedBss to its all-zero sentinel, zeros prop:fi.nexus.Wifi.SignalDbm / prop:fi.nexus.Wifi.Frequency, and drops prop:fi.nexus.Wifi.ScanResults — every Wi-Fi-off-related property agrees before the typed sig:fi.nexus.Wifi.StateChanged{state='disconnected', reason='rf_killed'} edge fires. (3) Since nexus-wifi 0.17.0, this is now also true at the wifi-backend layer: rfkill drives the internal WifiState to Disconnected{RfKilled}, which (a) is `is_permanent()` so the disconnect-cooldown sweep cannot auto-promote it back to Idle and (b) gates `request_scan` / `Wifi.Connect` / `Wifi.Roam` so they refuse rather than churn against a powered-off radio. A subsequent Powered=false→true does NOT carry the pre-power-off State forward; the wifi backend folds RfKilled to `idle` and the auto-select path kicks a fresh scan.

params.allow_roam: b — only honoured when RoamingMode == supplicant

attrs.completion_semantics: Returns the job_id immediately after auth/rate/feature/parse gates pass. ScanComplete fires exactly once per accepted call, on either the supplicant's ScanDone or a synchronous backend rejection. ResourceBusy (stacked-scan rejection) is no longer a synchronous error — it surfaces as ScanComplete(success=false, reason='busy').
attrs.retry_hint: RateLimited carries retry_after_ms; honour it. For ScanComplete(success=false, reason='busy'), wait at least 2s before re-issuing.

attrs.stickiness: Explicit Connect on a non-auto-connect profile makes it sticky until explicit Disconnect or daemon restart, even across transient Disconnected states.
attrs.completion_semantics: Returns the job_id immediately after auth/rate/feature gates pass. Exactly one ConnectComplete fires per Connect call. ConnectComplete is the **converged** terminal edge: success on a transition to Connected, or failure on a Disconnected{reason} whose wire reason is in the terminal set (credentials_invalid | rf_killed | supplicant_unavailable). Transient failures (handshake_timeout, ap_initiated, post_sleep_recovery, …) are swallowed — the wifi backend's sticky-retry path produces the eventual verdict (a successful Connected, or a credentials_invalid promotion after the BSSID failure threshold trips per DD-003 §6.3) and that is what fires ConnectComplete. An explicit Disconnect before the verdict resolves the job with reason='cancelled' from the Disconnect handler.

attrs.purpose: Tear down the current association on this Wi-Fi interface. Transitions the interface to State=disconnected and emits Interface.StateChanged / Wifi.StateChanged. Returns a job_id for the corresponding DisconnectComplete signal.

params_keys.pause_auto_connect: b — when true, also block the active profile from the daemon's auto-connect picker until daemon restart, an explicit Connect(profile), or a profile edit. Runtime-only; does NOT modify the on-disk Profile.Wifi.AutoConnect field. Default false.

attrs.durability: By default, transient — does not remove the stored profile and does not block auto-reconnect; the backend may auto-reconnect on the next scan tick if the profile has auto_connect=true and a matching BSS is in range. With params.pause_auto_connect=true, the disconnect also installs a session-only pause that survives across SetPowered toggles and adapter off/on cycles, but is cleared by daemon restart, by an explicit Connect(profile) on the same profile, by Profile.Update, or by Profile.Delete / Manager.RemoveProfile.
attrs.to_opt_out_persistently: Either Profile.Update with auto_connect=false (persistent, on-disk), or Manager.RemoveProfile / Profile.Delete (forget the profile).
attrs.completion_semantics: DisconnectComplete fires once when the supplicant teardown returns: success (reason='') or failure (reason='other') if the backend errored mid-teardown. Issuing Disconnect while a Connect job is in flight cancels that Connect with reason='cancelled' before the disconnect itself proceeds.

attrs.purpose: Reply to a NetworkRequest signal. Pass the network path back verbatim.

Terminal edge for an operator-initiated Wifi.Scan. Fires exactly once per accepted call (passive or active). job_id matches the value returned by Scan; results_count is the number of fi.nexus.ScanResult objects currently registered under <iface>/scan_result/ at completion time. reason is '' on success and one of busy | rf_killed | supplicant_unavailable | aborted | other on failure.
attrs.correlation: Match by job_id with the value returned by method:fi.nexus.Wifi.Scan.

attrs.purpose: Supplicant is requesting an out-of-band credential. Respond via Wifi.ProvideCredential.

Typed mirror of fi.nexus.Interface.StateChanged emitted on the same path with the same args and details schema. Provided so clients whose typed proxy stack reliably resolves per-technology signals but not the common fi.nexus.Interface signals can subscribe on the technology-specific channel.
attrs.details_schema: Same as Interface.StateChanged: reason (s), bssid (ay), ssid_bytes (ay), frequency (u), signal_dbm (i), security (s), profile (o) — keys present per the DD-006 §9 details table.
attrs.transition_only: Idempotent since nexus-dbus 0.13.2: a re-emission with the same (state, details) is suppressed daemon-side. The same dedup gate covers both Wifi.StateChanged and the mirrored Interface.StateChanged.
attrs.consistency: When this signal fires with state='connected', the daemon flushes pending PropertiesChanged for prop:fi.nexus.Wifi.Powered, prop:fi.nexus.Interface.OperState, prop:fi.nexus.Interface.Carrier first, then emits the typed StateChanged. Consumers that read those properties on the connected edge see consistent post-connect values rather than stale pre-connect ones.
attrs.fires_on_powered_false: Since nexus-dbus 0.14.0, every prop:fi.nexus.Wifi.Powered=false transition (rfkill engaged or operator write) synthesizes a StateChanged with new_state='disconnected' and details.reason='rf_killed'. The daemon also lands prop:fi.nexus.Wifi.ConnectedBss / SignalDbm / Frequency to their not-associated values and drops prop:fi.nexus.Wifi.ScanResults before this edge fires. Since nexus-wifi 0.17.0 the wifi backend independently emits the same edge from its own state-machine transition to Disconnected{RfKilled}; the dedup gate suppresses the duplicate, and a late-arriving wpa_supplicant `Disconnected{LocalRequest|other}` no longer overwrites the rf_killed reason on the wire. Consumers that need the rfkill-driven edge (vs. a backend-driven Disconnected) can still distinguish via this reason.

attrs.purpose: Terminal edge for an operator-initiated Wifi.Connect. Exactly one ConnectComplete fires per Connect job. job_id matches the value returned by Connect; success is true iff the interface reached Connected for the attempt.
attrs.ordering: Since nexus-dbus 0.13.2, a successful ConnectComplete fires *after* sig:fi.nexus.Wifi.StateChanged='connected' and *after* the PropertiesChanged that bring prop:fi.nexus.Wifi.Powered, prop:fi.nexus.Interface.OperState, and prop:fi.nexus.Interface.Carrier into a connected-consistent state. A consumer that reads any of those on the ConnectComplete edge sees the post-connect values.
attrs.fires_on: Connected → success, reason=''. Disconnected{reason} → fires only when the wire reason is in the terminal set: credentials_invalid (auth definitively failed, including BSSID-failure-threshold promotion), rf_killed (operator must un-kill RF), supplicant_unavailable (supplicant gone). Disconnect cancellation → reason='cancelled' (fired from the Disconnect handler before the disconnect proceeds).
attrs.transient_disconnects_swallowed: Disconnected{HandshakeTimeout | ApInitiated | Inactivity | ProtocolError | PostSleepRecovery | DriverWedge | Unspecified | Other} are NOT terminal — the wifi backend's cooldown + sticky-retry path continues, and the eventual converged transition (a successful Connected, or a CredentialsInvalid promotion after the BSSID failure threshold trips per DD-003 §6.3) is what fires ConnectComplete. Consumers should NOT special-case these reasons; before fi.nexus 0.13.1 they leaked through and required a 30 s connect-watchdog on the consumer side.
attrs.correlation: Match by job_id with the value returned by method:fi.nexus.Wifi.Connect.

attrs.purpose: Terminal edge for an operator-initiated Wifi.Disconnect. reason is '' on success (the operator asked) and 'other' when the backend failed mid-teardown.
attrs.correlation: Match by job_id with the value returned by method:fi.nexus.Wifi.Disconnect.
