flows.name: Discover the Nexus surface and subscribe to changes
preconditions: Connected to system bus
fi.nexus1 owns its name (auto-activated if needed)

steps.do: Call org.freedesktop.DBus.ObjectManager.GetManagedObjects on /fi/nexus1
steps.yields: Map of every Nexus object path -> {interfaceName: {propertyName: variant}}.

steps.do: Subscribe to InterfacesAdded and InterfacesRemoved on /fi/nexus1
Subscribe to PropertiesChanged with no path filter to receive all property updates
steps.tip: Filter by sender=fi.nexus1 to ignore unrelated bus traffic.

ui_notes: ObjectManager is the canonical truth. Manager.WifiProfiles, Wifi.ScanResults are convenience caches that may briefly lag — prefer ObjectManager for ordering-sensitive UI.
Hot properties (SignalDbm, Frequency, AgeMs) arrive at <= 1 Hz per object; render with that cadence in mind.

flows.name: Connect to a stored Wi-Fi profile by SSID
preconditions: A Wi-Fi profile exists for the target SSID
An interface with Kind=wifi is registered

steps.do: Manager.FindWifiProfile(ssid)
Manager.GetInterface(ifname)
Wifi.Connect(profile_path) on the interface object — capture the returned job_id

Wait for Wifi.ConnectComplete(job_id, success, reason) — this is the canonical 'did we get there' edge; replace any 30s connect-watchdog with this signal. As of fi.nexus 0.13.1 the daemon swallows transient disconnects (handshake_timeout, ap_initiated, …) and only fires ConnectComplete on the converged outcome, so consumers no longer need to debounce non-terminal failure reasons.
steps.expected_failures: success=false, reason in {credentials_invalid, rf_killed, supplicant_unavailable, cancelled}

steps.do: Optionally, for progress-UI animation, watch Wifi.StateChanged or fi.nexus.Interface.StateChanged on the interface path — both carry the same args and details

Once Wifi.ConnectComplete success has fired, render the IP rows (IPv4 / IPv6 address, gateway, DNS) on the connected card by following flow:read-ip-info-for-connected-iface — Nexus does NOT publish IP-layer state on fi.nexus1; addresses, routes, and DNS live on systemd-networkd and systemd-resolved per nexus-architecture.md ADR-001.

flows.name: Add a new Wi-Fi profile and connect

steps.do: Optionally Wifi.Scan to populate ScanResults so the UI can pick an SSID
Wait for Wifi.ScanComplete and read Wifi.ScanResults
Manager.AddWifiProfile(settings)
Wifi.Connect(profile_path) — explicit Connect bypasses auto_connect and is sticky. Capture the returned job_id.
Wait for Wifi.ConnectComplete(job_id, success, reason) — canonical terminal edge; do not roll a separate watchdog timer

Once ConnectComplete success has fired, render the IP rows on the connected card via flow:read-ip-info-for-connected-iface (systemd-networkd Manager.Describe + systemd-resolved Link.DNS). fi.nexus1 itself does not expose IP-layer state — see ADR-001.

ui_notes: On AlreadyExists, fetch the existing profile via FindWifiProfile and offer Profile.Update instead.
Credential strings are cleartext on the bus and encrypted on disk by the Profile Store. They never leave Nexus via Properties.Get.

flows.name: Build a Wi-Fi scan picker that updates live

steps.do: Subscribe to Wifi.ScanComplete on the interface path BEFORE issuing the scan to avoid a startup race
Trigger Wifi.Scan with empty params — capture the returned job_id

Wait for Wifi.ScanComplete(job_id, success, results_count, reason) — canonical completion edge. results_count is the on-bus number of fi.nexus.ScanResult objects under <iface>/scan_result/ at completion time. Failure reasons: busy | rf_killed | supplicant_unavailable | aborted | other.

(Parallel option for streaming-row UIs) Subscribe to InterfacesAdded/InterfacesRemoved under /fi/nexus1/interface/<ifname>/scan_result/ to render rows incrementally as BSSes are discovered, rather than waiting for ScanComplete to settle the list.
For each new path, GetAll on fi.nexus.ScanResult to populate the row
Subscribe to PropertiesChanged on each scan_result path; SignalDbm and AgeMs are hot (<=1Hz)
When a row disappears via InterfacesRemoved, drop it from the UI

ui_notes: ResourceBusy on Scan means the driver is busy — wait >=2s and retry.
RateLimited carries retry_after_ms; back off accordingly. Don't eat the user's screen with retries.

Default presentation: group scan_result objects client-side by (ScanResult.Ssid, ScanResult.SecurityOffered) and show one row per group, picking max(ScanResult.SignalDbm) for the displayed strength. This mirrors the ConnMan Service model (one entry per SSID+security, BSSID hidden) which most operators expect from a Wi-Fi picker. Nexus deliberately exposes the un-aggregated per-BSSID surface on iface:fi.nexus.ScanResult — keep that detail accessible behind a 'show APs' affordance for diagnostics, BSSID pinning (Profile.Wifi.BssidPreferred), blacklisting (Profile.Wifi.BssidBlacklist), and roaming UIs.

For the per-tick state-machine view (animating connecting → authenticating → handshaking → connected as the operator picks a row), prefer sig:fi.nexus.Wifi.StateChanged — it is the typed-signal alternative to subscribing PropertiesChanged on prop:fi.nexus.Wifi.State, which some typed-proxy stacks (e.g., Qt 6 QtDBus) coalesce or fail to deliver reliably for high-frequency property updates.

flows.name: Reply when wpa_supplicant asks for an OTP/PIN/passphrase mid-connect
preconditions: Wifi.State has reached authenticating

steps.do: Subscribe to Wifi.NetworkRequest before initiating Connect
When NetworkRequest(network, field, text) fires, surface 'text' to the operator
ui_notes: text is supplicant-supplied; show it as-is
field tells you which secret type to collect

steps.do: Wifi.ProvideCredential(network, field, value) — pass the network path back verbatim
Watch StateChanged: connecting->authenticating->handshaking->connected on success, or disconnected with reason=credentials_invalid on rejection

flows.name: Recover from credentials_invalid on a stored profile
flows.trigger: Manager.NotificationEvent kind=credentials_invalid OR Profile.CredentialsInvalid==true OR Profile.CredentialsInvalidChanged(true)

steps.do: Observe NotificationEvent
Prompt the operator for the new credential (passphrase/password/PIN)
Profile.Update(settings) on the profile path with the new credential field
Backend automatically clears CredentialsInvalid and retries on next auto-connect cycle. Watch CredentialsInvalidChanged(false) to confirm.

flows.name: Recover from a fail-fast 802.1X failure on ethernet
preconditions: Ethernet interface has dot1x.enabled=true and 802.1X authentication failed with bad_credentials or certificate_rejected (DD-002 §9.3 fail-fast)

steps.do: Observe NotificationEvent
Look up the profile path for this interface via Interface.ManagedProfile or Manager.EthernetProfiles.
Prompt the operator for the new credential. EAP-TLS profiles need a fresh client_cert / private_key / private_key_passwd; PEAP/TTLS profiles need a fresh password.
Profile.Update(settings) on the profile path with the new credential field.
Carrier cycle (or wait for natural recovery) re-runs the auth on the next link-up. Watch Interface.StateChanged on the interface path for state=authenticating then authenticated.

flows.note: EthernetProfile does not yet carry a CredentialsInvalid flag (the on-disk schema lacks the field), so there is no Profile.CredentialsInvalidChanged signal to confirm the recovery. The Manager.NotificationEvent above is the only authoritative event for ethernet credentials-invalid; the recovery-confirmation signal is Interface.StateChanged transitioning to authenticated.

flows.name: Disconnect from a Wi-Fi network and pause its auto-connect for this session
flows.trigger: Operator chose 'Disconnect (don't auto-rejoin)' or equivalent — a transient opt-out that should NOT touch the on-disk profile.
preconditions: A wifi-Kind interface is registered. An active connection on that interface (or no connection — the pause is then a no-op since the active-profile lookup misses).

steps.do: Call Wifi.Disconnect(params={'pause_auto_connect': true}) on the interface object. Tears down the current association and adds the active profile to the daemon's runtime paused-set. Capture the returned job_id.
Wait for Wifi.DisconnectComplete(job_id, success, reason) — canonical terminal edge. reason='' on success; 'other' on backend failure mid-teardown.

flows.note: The pause is runtime-only: it survives Wifi.SetPowered toggles and adapter off/on cycles but is cleared on daemon restart, on an explicit Connect to the same profile, on Profile.Update, and on RemoveProfile/Profile.Delete. Inspectable side-effect: the profile's Profile.Wifi.AutoConnect property still reads true on disk, but auto-select skips the profile until one of the clearing events fires. Use this when the operator wants 'don't connect right now' without committing to a persistent change. For persistent opt-out, edit Profile.Wifi.AutoConnect to false; for full removal, use flow:disconnect-and-forget-wifi. Issuing Disconnect while a Wifi.Connect is in flight also fires Wifi.ConnectComplete with reason='cancelled' for that connect's job_id.

flows.name: Disconnect from a Wi-Fi network and forget its profile
preconditions: A wifi-Kind interface is registered. A stored Wi-Fi profile exists for the network the operator wants to forget.

steps.do: Call Wifi.Disconnect on the interface object to tear down the current association. Skip this step if the interface is already idle/disconnected; calling it on an idle interface is harmless but no-op. Capture the returned job_id.
steps.note: Transient by itself — the backend may auto-reconnect on the next scan tick if the profile remains and auto_connect=true.

steps.do: Wait for Wifi.DisconnectComplete(job_id, success, reason) — canonical terminal edge for the disconnect call.
Resolve the stored profile's object path (from Manager.WifiProfiles, or the path captured when the profile was added).
Call Manager.RemoveProfile(path) (or equivalently Profile.Delete on the profile object) to forget the profile durably. Removes it from the in-memory cache and the on-disk profile store.
Watch ObjectManager.InterfacesRemoved on the profile path to confirm the profile was unregistered.

flows.note: Disconnect alone is reversible — the profile is still stored and the backend treats it as a candidate for the next scan/auto-connect cycle. RemoveProfile (or Profile.Delete on the profile object) is the durable opt-out. Order matters only for cleanliness: removing the profile while connected will also disconnect (per Manager.RemoveProfile.side_effect), but emitting Disconnect first gives the UI a clean state-change observation point. nexusctl wraps the two calls as 'wifi disconnect' and 'wifi forget <ssid|ulid>'.

flows.name: Discover and pair a Bluetooth device
preconditions: A bluetooth-Kind interface is registered and Powered

steps.do: Bluetooth.StartDiscovery({}) on the adapter path
Subscribe to ObjectManager InterfacesAdded for paths under <adapter-ifindex>/device/
When the operator picks one, Bluetooth.Pair(device) — capture the returned job_id
Subscribe to PairingStarted, PairingPrompt, PairingComplete on the adapter (filter by job_id)
On PairingPrompt, render UI based on kind (request_pin / request_passkey / display_passkey / request_confirmation / etc.)
Bluetooth.AnswerPairingPrompt(job_id, answer) with the variant matching kind
PairingComplete(job_id, success, reason) terminates the flow

ui_notes: All pairing signals fire on the adapter object, not the device object — subscribe at the adapter path and filter by job_id or device.
display_passkey / display_pin require an 'acknowledge' string answer so the backend can release BlueZ's Agent callback.
BLE devices may be Connect()ed without prior Pair() if the profile permits; Classic devices must Pair first.

flows.name: Subscribe to filtered GNSS fixes
preconditions: A gnss-Kind interface exists

steps.do: Locate the GNSS interface via Manager.Interfaces or ObjectManager filtering on Kind=gnss
Read Gnss.State to know whether tracking has begun
Subscribe to fi.nexus.Gnss.FixChanged for filtered, rate-capped fixes
Optionally subscribe to PropertiesChanged on Gnss.SatellitesInView/Used for a satellite count widget

ui_notes: LastFix is all zeros when no fix is held — branch on Gnss.State, never on the tuple values.
Mode 0=NoFix, 2=Fix2D, 3=Fix3D (gpsd convention).
GpsdConnected==false means fixes are stale; surface a connectivity hint to the operator.

flows.name: Toggle device power state

steps.do: Read Manager.PowerState (s)
Manager.SetPowerState(state)
Watch Manager.PowerStateChanged

ui_notes: active = full operation; background = scan/poll less; sleep = quiesce. Some backends throttle scan cadence based on this.

flows.name: Back up the profile store while frozen
preconditions: Caller has fi.nexus.admin

steps.do: Manager.FreezeForBackup() -> lease
Snapshot /var/lib/nexus/ contents via your backup tool
steps.tip: Lease TTL is 60 s; renew via Freeze->Release in a loop for longer operations.

steps.do: Manager.ReleaseBackupLease(lease)
steps.tip: Idempotent — safe to call in a finally block. NotFound on stale tokens is benign.

flows.name: Collect a redacted diagnostic bundle
preconditions: Caller has fi.nexus.admin

steps.do: Manager.CollectDiagnostics() -> bundle_fd
steps.tip: Read until EOF on the unix fd; close it afterwards.

steps.do: Stream the fd to disk or upload to support
steps.tip: Credentials are pre-redacted by the daemon; bundles can still be moderately sensitive (logs, metrics).

flows.name: Rotate the profile-store master key
preconditions: Caller has fi.nexus.admin

steps.do: Manager.RotateMasterKey() -> job_id
Subscribe to Manager.MasterKeyRotated and match by job_id

ui_notes: Duration scales with profile count (~10 ms per profile + ~100 ms fixed overhead).
Watch Manager.NotificationEvent kind=master_key_degraded if rotation fails — it indicates the store is running without decryption.

flows.name: Read IP / route / DNS for a connected interface (off-Nexus, on systemd-networkd + systemd-resolved)
flows.trigger: Want to render IPv4/IPv6 address, gateway, and DNS rows on a connected card after Wifi.ConnectComplete (or Ethernet authenticated/link_ready) has fired.
preconditions: Connected to the system bus.
systemd-networkd is running (the Nexus deployment requires it — see nexus-architecture.md ADR-001).
systemd-resolved is running for DNS rows. If it isn't, DNS rows are unavailable; the address/route rows still resolve via networkd.
flows._about: Nexus deliberately does NOT expose IP-layer state on fi.nexus1 — ADR-001 (`No built-in IP management`) keeps the daemon's surface at the kernel-carrier boundary. systemd-networkd and systemd-resolved both publish on the same system bus you already have open. This flow names the exact paths and methods so a UI can read addresses/routes/DNS without leaving D-Bus.

steps.do: Resolve the kernel ifindex for the interface you're rendering: read prop:fi.nexus.Interface.Ifindex.

Build the per-link object paths once. networkd: `/org/freedesktop/network1/link/_<ifindex>` (decimal int, underscore-prefixed). resolved: `/org/freedesktop/resolve1/link/_<ifindex>` (same convention).
steps.tip: Both paths use the same ifindex escape; compute once and reuse.

steps.do: Open subscriptions BEFORE the first read so a property change between reads doesn't slip through.
subscriptions: PropertiesChanged on /org/freedesktop/network1/link/_<ifindex> (member-filtered to interface=org.freedesktop.network1.Link). Triggers a re-DescribeLink() on each fire.
PropertiesChanged on /org/freedesktop/resolve1/link/_<ifindex> (member-filtered to interface=org.freedesktop.resolve1.Link). Triggers a DNS re-read.

steps.do: Call org.freedesktop.network1.Manager.DescribeLink(ifindex:i) on /org/freedesktop/network1. (Older systemds (<250) only expose the no-arg `Describe() -> (json:s)` manager-wide dump — fall back to that and pluck the entry whose `Index` matches your ifindex out of `JSON.Interfaces[]`.)
steps.yields: (json:s) — parse as JSON. Fields used by the connected-card recipe: `Addresses` (array of {Family:i, Address:ay, PrefixLength:u, Scope:i}); `Routes` (array of {Family:i, Destination:ay, DestinationPrefixLength:u, Gateway:ay, Scope:i, Type:i}); `DHCPv4`/`DHCPv6` (lease metadata — out of scope for the first cut, see notes).
steps.ipv4_address_extract: Filter Addresses where Family==2 (AF_INET) AND Scope==0 (RT_SCOPE_UNIVERSE / global). Decode 4-byte arrays to dotted-quad. Use PrefixLength as the subnet mask length.
steps.ipv4_gateway_extract: Filter Routes where Family==2 AND DestinationPrefixLength==0 (default route). Decode 4-byte Gateway. If multiple, prefer the lowest-Metric or first match — render whichever is winning the kernel's tie-break.
steps.ipv6_address_extract: Filter Addresses where Family==10 (AF_INET6). For the connected card, prefer Scope==0 (global) over Scope==253 (link). Render the link-local separately if at all.
steps.ipv6_gateway_extract: Filter Routes where Family==10 AND DestinationPrefixLength==0.

steps.do: Read DNS from systemd-resolved: Properties.Get on /org/freedesktop/resolve1/link/_<ifindex>, interface=org.freedesktop.resolve1.Link, property=DNS. When resolved is NOT on the bus (stripped-down rootfs without systemd-resolved), fall back to the per-link `DNS[]` array carried in the same DescribeLink JSON blob from the previous step — every entry is `{Family:i, Address:ay}`, decoded the same way.
steps.yields: a(iay) — array of (family, address-bytes). Decode family=2 → IPv4 dotted-quad, family=10 → IPv6 colon-hex. Show as a comma-joined list in the DNS row.

steps.do: On any subsequent PropertiesChanged from networkd's Link object, re-call DescribeLink(ifindex) and re-extract. On PropertiesChanged from resolved's Link object, re-read DNS.
steps.tip: Address state can churn during DHCP renewal — debounce the re-DescribeLink by ~200 ms if the PropertiesChanged firehose is noisy. networkd already coalesces per-state-summary changes.

ui_notes: Connect-flow ordering: subscribe BEFORE Wifi.Connect; first DescribeLink() lands AFTER Wifi.ConnectComplete success — but networkd's IPv4AddressState transition to 'routable' may fire either before or after ConnectComplete depending on DHCP timing. Treat the two as independent edges; the IP row renders when networkd tells you so.

On disconnected interfaces, DescribeLink() still works but Addresses[] is empty (or contains only link-local IPv6). Don't fall back to fi.nexus.Interface for an IP — there is no IP property there by design.

Match systemd version expectations: Manager.DescribeLink(ifindex) is available since systemd 250; the no-arg manager-wide Manager.Describe() has been around since systemd 219 and is the fallback path on older releases (Debian 12 / systemd 252 already exposes both). resolved.Link.DNS is available since systemd 232. Both are present on every systemd-based deployment Nexus targets.
Path-permissions: both calls are open to unprivileged readers on default systemd policy. Writes (Manager.Reload, etc.) are not used here.

Out of scope for this flow (file separately when the UI wants them): DHCP lease lifetime / renew timestamp (DHCPv4.LeaseEnd inside DescribeLink()), IPv6 SLAAC vs DHCPv6 distinguisher (Addresses[].Flags / DHCPv6 dict), and per-link metric stats.

queries.all_methods_on_interface: edges where rel=defines_method and from=<interface-id>; resolve to .nodes[?id==to]
queries.state_machine_for_kind: subgraph: nodes where type=State and id starts with state:<prefix>:; edges where rel=transitions_to between them
queries.object_paths_under_root: transitive closure of edges with rel=child_path starting at obj:/fi/nexus1

language_bindings.rust: zbus 5.x with #[proxy] generated from introspection XML.
language_bindings.python: jeepney (pure-Python, async-friendly) or sdbus; dbus-python is legacy.
language_bindings.c_cpp: GDBus or sd-bus. GDBus integrates with GMainLoop; sd-bus is lower-overhead.

consumer_recommendations.introspection: busctl introspect fi.nexus1 /fi/nexus1 to browse interactively at runtime. The committed introspection XML goldens (DD-006 §13) are the ground truth for compile-time codegen.
consumer_recommendations.subscriptions_first: Open all signal subscriptions BEFORE issuing the method that triggers them. Otherwise you can race past the first ScanCompleted, PairingPrompt, or StateChanged.
consumer_recommendations.hot_vs_cold: Treat SignalDbm/Frequency/AgeMs as a polled cache (~1Hz). Treat State/OperState/ManagedProfile as event-driven; act on every transition.
consumer_recommendations.object_path_strings: Never parse object paths to extract ifname or ulid for business logic — the escaping rules can produce surprises (eth0:1 -> eth0_3a1). Read Interface.Ifname or Profile.Id instead.
consumer_recommendations.rate_limit_etiquette: Honour retry_after_ms on RateLimited; do not retry on Timeout (the call may have succeeded — reconcile via state).
consumer_recommendations.ip_layer_data_source: fi.nexus1's surface stops at link-layer state — carrier, association, signal, security, profile management. IPv4 / IPv6 addresses, default gateway, and DNS are NOT exposed on fi.nexus.Interface; they live on systemd-networkd (org.freedesktop.network1) and systemd-resolved (org.freedesktop.resolve1) on the same system bus. This is a deliberate architectural delegation, ADR-001 in nexus-architecture.md (`No built-in IP management`). To render the IP rows on a connected card, read org.freedesktop.network1.Manager.DescribeLink(ifindex) for Addresses[] / Routes[] (or, on systemd <250, the no-arg Manager.Describe() and pluck the per-link entry from JSON.Interfaces[]) and org.freedesktop.resolve1.Link.DNS at /org/freedesktop/resolve1/link/_<ifindex> for DNS — see flow:read-ip-info-for-connected-iface and ui_design_patterns.connected_card_recipe for the full pattern. Subscribe PropertiesChanged on the per-link networkd / resolved objects for change notifications; do not poll.

open_questions: DD-004 (Bluetooth) is in flight; the BluetoothDevice profile path /fi/nexus1/profile/bluetooth/<ulid> is reserved but not yet served.
Per-device GNSS Activate/Deactivate methods are reserved for a post-v0.1 minor revision.

state_machines._about: UI-facing state-machine layer for designers. The graph's `nodes` (type=State) and `edges` (rel=transitions_to) carry structural topology; this section adds per-state UI semantics, transition triggers, and evidence signals. `node` fields cross-reference the graph IDs above.

wifi.supplicant_collapse_warning: When Wifi.Supplicant == 'iwd', the authenticating and handshaking states are NEVER observed — iwd reports the whole pre-connected window as connecting. UIs MUST treat connecting as covering 'attempting to associate, authenticate, and key' and not show three separate sub-stages unconditionally.

idle.ui_meaning: Radio is up and registered with the supplicant, no connection attempt in flight. Default landing state.

scanning.ui_meaning: Active or passive scan in progress. ScanResults will populate as BSSes are found; ScanCompleted fires when the scan settles.
scanning.typical_duration: 1–6 s active, up to ~10 s with all bands
ui_actions_available: Cancel (no API; scan is short — just wait)
Disable Powered to abort if user backs out

connecting.ui_meaning: Association in flight (Auth/Assoc frames being exchanged). On iwd, this state ALSO covers what wpa_supplicant would call authenticating + handshaking.
connecting.shows_progress: determinate if wpa_supplicant (3 sub-stages) / indeterminate if iwd
connecting.typical_duration: 1–3 s open, 2–6 s WPA2/3 PSK, 5–30 s Enterprise

authenticating.ui_meaning: WPA2/WPA3 4-way start, or EAP exchange for Enterprise. With iwd this is collapsed into connecting and never observed.
authenticating.shows_progress: indeterminate (Enterprise can pause for OTP/PIN — see NetworkRequest)
authenticating.typical_duration: 100 ms PSK, 1–10 s Enterprise (can stall awaiting NetworkRequest reply)
authenticating.interactive_branch: Wifi.NetworkRequest may fire here demanding an OTP/PIN/passphrase. Surface a credential prompt; reply via Wifi.ProvideCredential.

handshaking.ui_meaning: 4-way + group-key handshake. Skipped entirely for Open and OWE. Collapsed into connecting on iwd.

connected.ui_meaning: Associated, keyed, carrier up. systemd-networkd will start IP configuration around this point. Show SSID, signal bars (from SignalDbm), and frequency band.

roaming.ui_meaning: Switching to a better BSS (same SSID). Brief glitch in service; IP layer typically survives.
roaming.shows_progress: indeterminate; usually too short to render

disconnected.ui_meaning: Connection lost or refused. The 'reason' detail decides whether the state is transient (will cool down to idle and retry) or permanent (waits for operator).

transitions.trigger: auto-connect after profile match on cached scan
transitions.ui_note: User did not act — show progress without dismissing any open picker.

transitions.trigger: method:fi.nexus.Wifi.Roam OR supplicant-driven roam OR Nexus signal-degraded eval

transitions.ui_note: After cool-down, the backend will scan again automatically — UI can stay on the network screen and watch for reconnect.

transitions.trigger: operator Connect or sticky-profile auto-retry after cool-down

ui_guidance: Reduce State to a 4-state UI badge: { idle, scanning } → 'Ready'; { connecting, authenticating, handshaking } → 'Connecting…'; { connected } → 'Connected'; { roaming } → 'Reassociating…'; { disconnected } → 'Disconnected' (or 'Sign-in required' if reason is permanent).
Always read details.reason on disconnected. Permanent reasons (CredentialsInvalid) need a recovery affordance NOW; transient reasons need only a brief 'reconnecting…' note while cool-down elapses.

Wifi.NetworkRequest can fire mid-authenticating with no state change — subscribe BEFORE calling Connect, or you'll miss the prompt. Render a modal credential dialog and reply via Wifi.ProvideCredential.
Treat SignalDbm < -75 dBm as 'weak' visualization; it updates at <=1 Hz so animations should not assume sub-second cadence.
Wifi.Powered=false produces RfKilled disconnects; surface a top-level 'Wi-Fi off' affordance distinct from per-network state.

Picker aggregation: group scan_result objects by (Ssid, SecurityOffered), pick max(SignalDbm) per group, render one row per group. Mirrors the ConnMan Service model that operators expect. Keep per-BSSID detail (iface:fi.nexus.ScanResult) accessible behind a 'show APs' affordance for diagnostics, BssidPreferred pinning, and BssidBlacklist editing.

Signal bucketing for bars: SignalDbm >= -55 → 4 bars (excellent); -55 to -65 → 3 bars (good); -65 to -75 → 2 bars (fair); < -75 → 1 bar (weak). Apply the same buckets in the picker (per-row max(SignalDbm)) and on the connected pill (Wifi.SignalDbm).

Security badge from ScanResult.SecurityOffered: empty or ['open'] → no lock; ['owe'] → padlock + 'Enhanced Open'; ['wpa2-psk'|'wpa3-psk'|both] → padlock; ['wpa2-eap'|'wpa3-eap'|both] → padlock + 'Enterprise'. When both wpa2 and wpa3 are advertised, label by the strongest mode (wpa3) since that's what the supplicant will negotiate.

ScanResult.AgeMs > 30000 means the BSS hasn't been heard on the most recent scan tick — fade or move to a 'last seen' bucket rather than dropping it; the next scan can refresh it. AgeMs is hot-coalesced (~1Hz), so don't bind it to a high-rate animation.

Supplicant collapse (also see supplicant_collapse_warning): branch the connect-progress UI on Wifi.Supplicant. wpa_supplicant gives you connecting → authenticating → handshaking → connected (3 sub-stages worth showing on Enterprise). iwd reports the entire pre-connected window as connecting — show a single indeterminate 'Connecting…' indicator and don't promise sub-stages.

Roaming should be near-silent in the steady-state UI: don't dismiss the connected screen on Wifi.RoamStarted/State=roaming; the IP layer typically survives a sub-second reassociation. Surface roam events only in a diagnostics view, or as a brief inline 'Reassociating…' chip that doesn't displace content.

Hidden networks: visible scan_result objects only carry the broadcast set. To connect to a hidden SSID, the operator types the SSID into 'Add network' and the profile is created with hidden=true; do not require a scan_result match for that path.

unavailable.ui_meaning: Kernel sees the adapter but BlueZ has not exposed it. Common at startup before BlueZ is up, or during BlueZ restart.
unavailable.typical_duration: <5 s at boot; possibly longer if BlueZ is misconfigured

present.ui_meaning: Adapter visible to BlueZ but Powered=false. Show a big 'Turn on Bluetooth' toggle.

powered.ui_meaning: Radio is up, no discovery in flight. Known/paired devices can be connected; new devices need StartDiscovery.

discovering.ui_meaning: Discovery session is active. New device objects appear via ObjectManager InterfacesAdded; their RSSI updates live.
discovering.typical_duration: Until StopDiscovery (no automatic timeout from Nexus; BlueZ may stop after ~12 s by default but Nexus session can re-arm)
discovering.concurrency_note: Discovering reflects BlueZ's aggregate flag — another client could be discovering. NexusDiscovering tells you whether YOUR session is active.

gone.ui_meaning: Adapter physically removed (USB unplug) or BlueZ object disappeared. The adapter's interface object will be removed from ObjectManager momentarily.

transitions.ui_note: Powered/Discoverable/Pairable/Discovering/NexusDiscovering have no live-update signal of their own — only the derived State gets StateChanged. Re-Get the individual property after observing StateChanged if you need its exact value.
Could fire from any state; treat as terminal — clear adapter UI, await re-discovery.

transitions.trigger: BlueZ appears with adapter already powered
transitions.ui_note: Observed as ObjectManager.InterfacesAdded (Unavailable->Present) then sig:fi.nexus.Bluetooth.StateChanged(state='powered') (Present->Powered); not a single atomic transition.

ui_guidance: Top-level Bluetooth toggle binds to fi.nexus.Bluetooth.Powered (read/write). Disable the toggle while State==unavailable; show 'Starting Bluetooth…' instead.
Distinguish Discovering (any client is scanning) from NexusDiscovering (your scan is the active one) when deciding whether YOUR Stop button is meaningful.
Paired-device list = filter Bluetooth.KnownDevices by BluetoothDevice.Paired==true. Discovered-device list = the rest, while State==discovering.

Subscribe to sig:fi.nexus.Bluetooth.StateChanged on the adapter object for live Present/Powered/Discovering transitions instead of polling State. Nexus does not gate emission on whether a UI is 'watching' — subscribe (AddMatch) while the Bluetooth page is visible and drop the subscription when it isn't; that alone controls the traffic you receive.

discovered.ui_meaning: Device seen during discovery. Not paired. May be a beacon (no GAP name) or a pairable peripheral.
discovered.is_steady: transient unless the adapter remains in discovery

pairing.ui_meaning: Pairing exchange in flight. The Agent will deliver PairingPrompt signals that need operator response.
pairing.typical_duration: 2–30 s depending on prompt type and operator response time
pairing.interactive_branch: MUST handle PairingPrompt(job_id, kind, data) and reply via AnswerPairingPrompt before BlueZ's Agent timeout (default 60 s). job_id ties prompts to this device's Pair() call.

paired.ui_meaning: Bonded but not currently connected. Show a 'Connect' button.
ui_actions_available: Trust toggle (Trusted=true skips per-connection authorization later)

connecting.ui_meaning: BlueZ Connect call outstanding. Service profiles are being set up.
connecting.typical_duration: 1–10 s depending on profile (HFP/A2DP slow, GATT-only fast)

connected.ui_meaning: Services are available. UUIDs property lists what's exposed (SDP for Classic, GATT for BLE).

disconnecting.ui_meaning: Explicit disconnect in flight. Brief; usually completes in <1 s.

failed.ui_meaning: Last pair or connect failed. Stays here until operator action — does NOT auto-retry.

removed.ui_meaning: Device removed from BlueZ registry. Object will be removed from ObjectManager momentarily.

transitions.ui_note: BluetoothDevice.State does not surface a 'pairing' value today — nexus-dbus only ever derives discovered/paired/connected from steady-state BlueZ properties. Track 'pairing' as UI-local state driven by PairingStarted, not by watching State.

transitions.trigger: Pair() error or Agent prompt cancelled
transitions.evidence_signal: sig:fi.nexus.Bluetooth.PairingComplete(job_id, success=false, reason in {rejected, timeout, auth_failed, connection_failed, other})

transitions.ui_note: BluetoothDevice.State does not surface a 'connecting' value today; track it as UI-local state between calling Connect and observing ConnectionChanged/StateChanged.
Classic devices return NotPaired here; only offer Connect from Discovered for BLE.
BluetoothDevice.State does not surface a 'disconnecting' value today; track it as UI-local state between calling Disconnect and observing ConnectionChanged/StateChanged.

transitions.trigger: Peer-initiated disconnect (link supervision timeout, peer power-off)

transitions.ui_note: Treat as terminal from any state. Drop the device from the UI.

ui_guidance: PairingPrompt is the linchpin of pairing UX. Subscribe at the ADAPTER object before calling Pair (the prompt fires on the adapter, not the device — filter by job_id and data.device).

Render PairingPrompt UI per kind: request_pin → numeric/text entry; request_passkey → 6-digit numeric entry; display_passkey/display_pin → read-only 'enter this on the other device' screen with an Acknowledge button (answer 's':'acknowledge'); request_confirmation → 'do these match?' yes/no with the passkey from data.passkey; request_authorization/authorize_service → simple yes/no.
BlueZ's Agent has a default 60 s prompt timeout. If the user is unresponsive, the pairing fails with reason='timeout' on PairingComplete. Show a countdown if your UX requires it.
Always offer a Cancel button — answer 's':'cancel' aborts any prompt regardless of kind.

BluetoothDevice.Trusted=true on a paired device tells BlueZ to skip per-connection authorization. Useful for headphones/keyboards the user plainly trusts; surface as a 'Trust this device' checkbox on the paired-device detail screen.

Subscribe to sig:fi.nexus.BluetoothDevice.StateChanged and sig:fi.nexus.BluetoothDevice.ConnectionChanged on each device object you're displaying instead of polling — both fire only on a real transition (no dupes on redelivery). Connecting/Disconnecting/Pairing are UI-local states you track between the method call and the resulting signal; State itself only ever shows discovered/paired/connected.
Failed is sticky — UI must offer Retry or Forget. Do NOT silently auto-retry; the failure may have been a wrong PIN that requires fresh user input.

gnss.global_concern: fi.nexus.Gnss.GpsdConnected is a backend-wide flag, not per-device. State alone does not tell you whether gpsd is reachable — read GpsdConnected too. A device sitting in Acquiring with GpsdConnected=false means 'fixes can't arrive yet because gpsd is down', not 'sky is blocked'.

pending.ui_meaning: GNSS device discovered but not yet registered with gpsd. Brief; transitions to acquiring as soon as the backend talks to gpsd.
pending.typical_duration: <1 s if gpsd is up; otherwise blocks until GpsdConnected flips true

acquiring.ui_meaning: Registered with gpsd, no qualifying fix yet. Cold-start can legitimately take minutes — do not show 'failed' prematurely.
acquiring.shows_progress: indeterminate; satellite count is the meaningful progress signal
acquiring.typical_duration: 30 s warm start, up to 5 min cold start (no almanac, weak signal)
live_telemetry: Gnss.SatellitesInView (rises as the sky search progresses)
acquiring.ui_guidance: Show satellites_in_view as the progress hint. 'Searching for satellites… 4 in view, 0 used' is more useful than a generic spinner.

tracking.ui_meaning: Receiving fixes that pass the configured quality threshold. Steady-state — render position, velocity, error.
tracking.ui_guidance: Update the position display on FixChanged events (rate-capped by the backend). horizontal_error_m maps cleanly to a confidence radius on a map.

degraded.ui_meaning: Was tracking, signal deteriorated — no qualifying fix for >= 30 s OR repeatedly below quality threshold. Last good fix is still readable from LastFix.
degraded.ui_guidance: Show last-known position with a 'last updated N seconds ago' label, plus a degraded indicator (e.g., dashed accuracy ring). Do NOT show a hard error — degraded is normal in tunnels, urban canyons, indoors.

transitions.trigger: Backend registered the device with gpsd
First TPV that passes quality threshold

transitions.ui_note: Treat as 'still searching' visually — do not show an error.

transitions.trigger: TPV stall (>= tpv_stall_timeout_s, default 30 s) OR fix quality below threshold

ui_guidance: Render GpsdConnected as a separate top-level health pill ('GPS service offline' vs 'GPS service running'). Don't conflate it with per-device state.
Mode tells you fix dimensionality: 0=NoFix (don't render coordinates), 2=Fix2D (render position; altitude is undefined), 3=Fix3D (full position+altitude).

horizontal_error_m is 95% CI in meters — render as the radius of a confidence circle on maps. vertical_error_m may be 0.0 if the receiver doesn't supply it; treat 0.0 as 'not reported', not 'perfect'.
satellites_used is the most legible progress indicator while in acquiring. Most consumer modules need ~4 satellites for a Fix2D, ~5+ for Fix3D.
track_deg is undefined at zero speed; many receivers report 0.0 in that case. Don't render a heading arrow when speed_mps < ~0.5.

ui_design_patterns._about: Cross-cutting UI design recipes that span Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and GNSS. nexusd already encodes the domain knowledge — these recipes lift the implications into UI form so implementers can apply them directly without re-deriving from the DDs. Use alongside `state_machines.<tech>.ui_guidance` (per-state details) and `command_sequences.*` (turn-by-turn scripts).

notification_event_dispatch.title: How to render each Manager.NotificationEvent kind
notification_event_dispatch.purpose: NotificationEvent is the operator-facing alert channel. The right UI surface depends on whether the event is recoverable, whether it's per-interface or system-wide, and whether the operator can act on it now.
rules: Subscribe to fi.nexus.Manager.NotificationEvent at /fi/nexus1 once at app start; route by `kind`. Treat unknown kinds as a generic toast carrying `kind` + the formatted `data` dict — never drop them.

Group by recoverability: recoverable kinds (credentials_invalid, eth_credentials_invalid, profile_corrupt) belong in the fix-feed (see ui:fix_feed). Informational kinds (subsystem_unavailable, subsystem_recovered) belong in a transient banner. Admin-level kinds (master_key_degraded) belong in a settings/security pane and SHOULD persist until acknowledged.
Attach the recovery affordance from the kind's `remediation` attr — don't ask the operator to figure out what to do.

kind:credentials_invalid.surface: fix-feed item + optional toast on first arrival

kind:eth_credentials_invalid.title_copy: 'Network sign-in rejected on <ifname>' (subtitle: reason → 'wrong password' for bad_credentials, 'certificate rejected' for certificate_rejected)
kind:eth_credentials_invalid.primary_action: 'Update credentials' → opens EAP-method-appropriate form → Profile.Update on the Ethernet profile

kind:subsystem_unavailable.surface: top-of-screen banner scoped to the affected technology
kind:subsystem_unavailable.title_copy: subsystem='gpsd' → 'GPS service offline'; subsystem='wpa_supplicant' → 'Wi-Fi service offline'; subsystem='bluez' → 'Bluetooth service offline'
kind:subsystem_unavailable.primary_action: (none — recovery is automatic) ; show a 'Diagnostics' link to a logs view

kind:subsystem_recovered.surface: clear the matching subsystem_unavailable banner; optional brief 'service restored' toast

kind:master_key_degraded.surface: persistent admin-level alert in security/settings pane (NOT a transient toast)
kind:master_key_degraded.title_copy: 'Profile encryption key degraded — saved credentials may be at risk'

kind:auth_backend_unavailable.surface: (reserved — not currently emitted; see node attrs) ; if observed, treat as subsystem_unavailable for the named backend

error_to_user_copy.title: Translating fi.nexus.Error.* into operator-facing copy and recovery affordances
error_to_user_copy.purpose: D-Bus errors on the public surface have well-defined semantics. The same error means the same thing across backends — operators benefit from consistent copy and a consistent recovery affordance.
rules: Always render the operator-facing copy, never the raw error name. Log the error name + path + method to a diagnostics view.

Bucket by recoverability: 'retry now' (ResourceBusy, Timeout-with-care), 'wait then retry' (RateLimited), 'fix input' (InvalidArgument, AlreadyExists, NotPaired), 'fix permissions' (AuthFailed), 'unrecoverable in this UI' (FeatureDisabled, Unsupported, BluezUnavailable, SupplicantUnavailable).
Special case Timeout: the call may have actually succeeded server-side. Do NOT auto-retry blindly — reconcile via state (re-read Properties, re-walk ObjectManager) before deciding.

err:fi.nexus.Error.NotFound.copy: context-dependent: 'No such network', 'No such interface', 'Profile no longer exists'

err:fi.nexus.Error.AlreadyExists.copy: 'A profile for this network already exists'

err:fi.nexus.Error.InvalidArgument.copy: 'That doesn\'t look right' + the field that failed validation if known
err:fi.nexus.Error.InvalidArgument.affordance: highlight the offending field; let the operator fix it

err:fi.nexus.Error.InvalidState.copy: 'Can\'t do that right now' + the state we\'re in
err:fi.nexus.Error.InvalidState.affordance: wait for the state to advance, then retry; never auto-retry inside the same state

err:fi.nexus.Error.AuthFailed.copy: 'Sign in as administrator to do this'
err:fi.nexus.Error.AuthFailed.affordance: see ui:permissions_handling — trigger a polkit auth agent prompt where supported, else block with a hint

err:fi.nexus.Error.ResourceBusy.affordance: wait >=2 s and retry once; surface only if a second attempt also fails

err:fi.nexus.Error.RateLimited.copy: 'Too many requests — try again in <retry_after_ms / 1000> s'
err:fi.nexus.Error.RateLimited.affordance: respect retry_after_ms; render a countdown if the UI is blocking on the call

err:fi.nexus.Error.FeatureDisabled.affordance: disable the feature surface entirely; no retry path

err:fi.nexus.Error.Timeout.affordance: DO NOT auto-retry; re-read state and decide based on observed reality

err:fi.nexus.Error.SupplicantUnavailable.copy: 'Wi-Fi service is starting up — please wait'
err:fi.nexus.Error.SupplicantUnavailable.affordance: auto-clear when subsystem_recovered fires; no manual retry needed

err:fi.nexus.Error.IoError.affordance: single retry; on second failure escalate to diagnostics

err:fi.nexus.Error.CryptoError.affordance: tie to master_key_degraded if that notification has fired; otherwise treat as IoError

err:fi.nexus.Error.Unsupported.affordance: disable the affordance permanently for this device

err:fi.nexus.Error.UnknownDevice.affordance: remove from list, re-scan if appropriate

err:fi.nexus.Error.UnknownPairingJob.affordance: drop any open prompt UI; pairing must be restarted

err:fi.nexus.Error.NotPowered.affordance: show a 'Turn on' toggle that writes the relevant Powered property

err:fi.nexus.Error.ConnectionFailed.copy: 'Couldn\'t connect — peer may be out of range'
err:fi.nexus.Error.ConnectionFailed.affordance: single retry; do NOT auto-retry repeatedly (peer-side issue)

fix_feed.title: Build a 'fix-feed' that aggregates recoverable problems
fix_feed.purpose: Operators benefit from a single list of 'things that need my attention' rather than scattered toasts. Several signals across backends collectively form this feed.

feed_sources.source: Profile.CredentialsInvalidChanged(true) on a Wi-Fi profile (mirrors the notification — use whichever arrives first)
Interface.StateChanged with state=disconnected and details.reason in {credentials_invalid, server_unreachable, certificate_rejected} that has persisted past cool-down
BluetoothDevice.State==failed (sticky failure that does not auto-retry — see state_machines.bluetooth_device.states.failed)

row_template.id: stable composite (row_kind + profile_path or ifname or device_path) so re-emissions deduplicate
row_template.title: operator-facing summary (use error_to_user_copy / notification_event_dispatch.dispatch_table)
row_template.primary_action: the recovery affordance from the dispatch_table entry
row_template.secondary_action: 'Dismiss' (transient — the row reappears if the underlying condition is re-asserted)
row_template.auto_clear_on: the inverse signal (CredentialsInvalidChanged(false), state advances to authenticated/connected, BluetoothDevice.Forget called, etc.)

fix_feed.ordering: Sort by first-seen-time desc with severity boost (master_key_degraded > credentials_invalid > profile_corrupt > bluetooth-failure). Don't reshuffle on every event; debounce.

connection_status_reduce.title: Single 'are we online?' badge across Ethernet + Wi-Fi
connection_status_reduce.purpose: Operators want one yes/no answer for connectivity. Reducing across multiple interfaces consistently is the difference between a UI that feels coherent and one that contradicts itself.
recipe: Walk all Interface objects via ObjectManager. For each Kind=ethernet, read Ethernet.State; for each Kind=wifi, read Wifi.State.
An interface is 'connected' when: Kind=ethernet AND State==link_ready (no 802.1X) OR State==authenticated (with 802.1X); or Kind=wifi AND State==connected.

If ANY interface is connected → badge='online', preferred_kind=ethernet over wifi if both. If NONE connected but ANY is in connecting/authenticating/handshaking → badge='connecting'. Otherwise badge='offline'.
Subscribe to fi.nexus.Interface.StateChanged with no path filter; recompute the reduce on every transition. Hot-property changes (SignalDbm, Frequency) MUST NOT trigger badge recomputation.
do_not: Don't infer connectivity from carrier alone — 802.1X-required networks have carrier without connectivity.
Don't use OperState as the truth source — it reflects kernel link state, not application-layer readiness. State is the right property.
Don't poll. The signal-driven reduce is sub-millisecond on real hardware.

connected_card_recipe.title: Render an iOS-style 'connected network' detail card
connected_card_recipe.purpose: Operators expect a familiar row order on the connected detail card (Wi-Fi or Ethernet). The data is split across three D-Bus services on the same system bus: fi.nexus1 (link-layer + signal/security), org.freedesktop.network1 (IP address + routes), and org.freedesktop.resolve1 (DNS). This recipe encodes the canonical row order and points at the right source for each row.
preconditions: The interface is in the 'connected' state — Wi-Fi: prop:fi.nexus.Wifi.State == 'connected'; Ethernet: prop:fi.nexus.Ethernet.State == 'link_ready' (no 802.1X) or 'authenticated' (with 802.1X).
systemd-networkd and systemd-resolved are running on the same system bus (true on every Nexus deployment per ADR-001).

row_order_top_to_bottom.source: prop:fi.nexus.Wifi.ConnectedBss → ssid_utf8_lossy field. Display the lossy string; keep the raw ssid_bytes for matching.
row_order_top_to_bottom.live_update: PropertiesChanged on fi.nexus.Wifi.ConnectedBss (rare — fires on roam).
Hot — coalesced PropertiesChanged at <=1 Hz; or sig:fi.nexus.Wifi.SignalLevel for level-change spikes.
row_order_top_to_bottom.render: Bar count from dBm thresholds (>=-55 = 4 bars, -55..-65 = 3, -65..-75 = 2, < -75 = 1). 2.4G/5G/6G band tag from frequency.
Lock icon for any non-open value; copy-text matches the operator's vocabulary ('WPA2', 'WPA3', 'Enterprise').

row_order_top_to_bottom.source: prop:fi.nexus.Wifi.ConnectedBss → bssid:ay (decode 6 bytes to colon-MAC, e.g. 8a:78:48:f0:12:ea) + frequency:u. Channel = the same freq→channel lookup the scan picker uses (2412→1, 2437→6, 5180→36, 5260→52, 5745→149, 5955→1 for 6 GHz with operating-class context, etc.).
row_order_top_to_bottom.render: Two lines: 'BSSID  aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff' and 'Channel  N (2.4 / 5 / 6 GHz)'. iOS does not surface BSSID on the public card; embedded operators routinely need it for roaming, BSSID pinning (Profile.Wifi.BssidPreferred), blacklisting (Profile.Wifi.BssidBlacklist), and field diagnostics — expose it under a 'Show details' / 'Advanced' disclosure rather than hiding it.
row_order_top_to_bottom.live_update: Same PropertiesChanged on Wifi.ConnectedBss as the Network-name row — fires on roam, so the BSSID/channel updates atomically with the rest of the card.

row_order_top_to_bottom.row: Other APs for this SSID (Wi-Fi roaming / diagnostics — advanced disclosure)
row_order_top_to_bottom.source: Filter prop:fi.nexus.Wifi.ScanResults: GetAll fi.nexus.ScanResult on each path, keep entries where ScanResult.Ssid equals the connected ConnectedBss.ssid_bytes (byte-equal, not string-equal — handles non-UTF-8 SSIDs), and drop the entry whose ScanResult.Bssid equals the connected BSSID. Sort the remainder by ScanResult.SignalDbm descending.
row_order_top_to_bottom.render: Stacked rows: 'aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff  Ch 36 (5 GHz)  −67 dBm'. Empty list is a normal state — most home deployments have one AP per SSID. Tap-to-pin opens flow:wifi-bssid-pinning (writes Profile.Wifi.BssidPreferred = MAC and re-Connects).
row_order_top_to_bottom.live_update: Driven by ObjectManager InterfacesAdded/Removed on /fi/nexus1/interface/<ifname>/scan_result/* and per-row PropertiesChanged on each ScanResult object. The list freshness is the freshness of the last Wi-Fi scan; surface a 'Last scanned: Ns ago' affordance derived from min(ScanResult.AgeMs).

row_order_top_to_bottom.source: Off-Nexus: org.freedesktop.network1.Manager.DescribeLink(ifindex) → JSON.Addresses[] with Family==2 (IPv4) and Scope==0 (global). See flow:read-ip-info-for-connected-iface.
row_order_top_to_bottom.render: '192.0.2.42 / 24' — dotted-quad + PrefixLength as CIDR. If multiple global IPv4 addresses, render the first; show a 'show all' affordance only if the device has multi-address use cases.

row_order_top_to_bottom.source: Same DescribeLink() blob — derive from the same Addresses[] entry's PrefixLength (e.g. 24 → 255.255.255.0). Not a separate D-Bus field.
row_order_top_to_bottom.render: Dotted-quad. Some operators prefer the CIDR-only display (collapsing IP + Subnet into one row); pick one and stay consistent.

row_order_top_to_bottom.source: Off-Nexus: org.freedesktop.network1.Manager.DescribeLink(ifindex) → JSON.Routes[] with Family==2 AND DestinationPrefixLength==0. Decode the Gateway 4-byte array.
row_order_top_to_bottom.render: Dotted-quad. Empty when no default route via this interface (rare on a 'connected' Wi-Fi card; common on a secondary management link).

row_order_top_to_bottom.source: Off-Nexus: org.freedesktop.resolve1.Link at /org/freedesktop/resolve1/link/_<ifindex>, property DNS (a(iay)). Fallback: when resolved is not running, the same DescribeLink() blob from networkd carries a per-link `DNS[]` array (entries `{Family:i, Address:ay}`); use it for the DNS row.
row_order_top_to_bottom.render: Comma-joined list of decoded addresses. If the list is empty, fall back to the Manager-level resolved DNS or hide the row entirely — don't render a literal '(none)' on what is normally a working connection.
row_order_top_to_bottom.live_update: PropertiesChanged on the resolved Link object (or, on the networkd-DNS fallback, on the networkd Link object).

row_order_top_to_bottom.row: IPv6 address (if present and the UI shows v6)
row_order_top_to_bottom.render: Prefer Scope==0 (global) over Scope==253 (link-local). Render the link-local separately under a 'show details' disclosure if at all.

row_order_top_to_bottom.source: method:fi.nexus.Wifi.Disconnect (Wi-Fi) — returns a job_id; resolve via sig:fi.nexus.Wifi.DisconnectComplete. For Ethernet, there is no direct Disconnect — operator removes the profile via Manager.RemoveProfile or toggles Powered.
row_order_top_to_bottom.tap_action: Wi-Fi: Wifi.Disconnect({}) and follow flow:disconnect-and-pause-wifi if the operator picks the 'don't auto-rejoin' variant.

row_order_top_to_bottom.source: Composite: Wifi.Disconnect → Manager.RemoveProfile (or Profile.Delete on the profile object).

subscriptions_needed: fi.nexus1: PropertiesChanged on the fi.nexus.Wifi (or fi.nexus.Ethernet) interface object. Drives Signal / Security / State rows.
fi.nexus1: sig:fi.nexus.Interface.StateChanged on the same path, OR sig:fi.nexus.Wifi.StateChanged for the typed mirror — recipients of either should ignore the other to avoid double-counting.
network1: PropertiesChanged on /org/freedesktop/network1/link/_<ifindex>. Triggers a re-Describe() and re-render of IP / Subnet / Router rows.
resolve1: PropertiesChanged on /org/freedesktop/resolve1/link/_<ifindex>. Triggers a re-read of DNS row only.
do_not: Don't poll. Every row above is event-driven. Polling Describe() in a tight loop is wasted CPU on the device.

Don't expect fi.nexus.Interface.* properties to grow IPv4Addresses / Ipv4Gateway / Ipv4DnsServers — Nexus deliberately does not publish IP-layer state. ADR-001 (`No built-in IP management`) keeps the daemon's surface at the kernel-carrier boundary; the IP rows live on networkd / resolved.

Don't conflate 'connected' (Wifi.State or Ethernet.State) with 'online' (networkd OnlineState). A network can be associated and keyed without a working DHCP lease. The connected card should render with whatever IP state networkd has at the moment, even if that's 'no IPv4 yet'.

alternative_aps_for_connected_ssid.title: Enumerate alternative APs (BSSes) visible for the connected SSID
alternative_aps_for_connected_ssid.purpose: On the connected card's 'Show details' / 'Advanced' disclosure, surface every BSS in the current scan cache that advertises the same SSID as the one we're associated to. Operators use this for roaming diagnostics ('why am I stuck on the weak AP?'), BSSID pinning (Profile.Wifi.BssidPreferred), and BSSID blacklisting (Profile.Wifi.BssidBlacklist). It is the same un-aggregated view the scan picker hides behind 'show APs' (see flow:scan-picker-ui ui_notes — 'Default presentation' bullet).
preconditions: prop:fi.nexus.Wifi.State == 'connected' (otherwise the 'connected SSID' is undefined — fall back to a plain scan list).
A recent Wifi.Scan has populated prop:fi.nexus.Wifi.ScanResults. Stale caches are normal — surface min(ScanResult.AgeMs) so the operator can decide whether to retrigger Wifi.Scan.
alternative_aps_for_connected_ssid._about: Nexus exposes the per-BSSID surface deliberately: each scan result is its own object at /fi/nexus1/interface/<ifname>/scan_result/<bssid> implementing iface:fi.nexus.ScanResult. The connected-card's 'connected BSS' is just one row from prop:fi.nexus.Wifi.ConnectedBss; the alternative-APs list is the rest of the scan, filtered to the same SSID.

lookup_recipe.do: Read prop:fi.nexus.Wifi.ConnectedBss → ssid_bytes (the raw ay), bssid (the connected MAC), frequency (the connected channel).
lookup_recipe.tip: Use ssid_bytes for the match key, NOT ssid_utf8_lossy — non-UTF-8 SSIDs are rare but legal and a lossy decode collapses distinct hidden bytes.

lookup_recipe.do: Read prop:fi.nexus.Wifi.ScanResults → array of object paths. Or, for streaming UIs, listen to ObjectManager InterfacesAdded/Removed under /fi/nexus1/interface/<ifname>/scan_result/.

For each path, GetAll on iface:fi.nexus.ScanResult. Keep the entries where ScanResult.Ssid (ay) equals ConnectedBss.ssid_bytes byte-for-byte and ScanResult.Bssid (ay) does NOT equal ConnectedBss.bssid.
Sort the remaining entries by ScanResult.SignalDbm descending. Render BSSID, channel (derived from ScanResult.Frequency), signal (dBm + bar-count), and security badge (ScanResult.SecurityOffered).

Subscribe PropertiesChanged on each kept ScanResult path so signal/age update live (each ScanResult emits coalesced PropertiesChanged at <=1 Hz — see edge `prop:fi.nexus.ScanResult.AgeMs rel=coalescing_class to coalesce:hot`).

tap_actions: Tap an alternative BSSID → 'Pin to this AP': open the active profile, write Profile.Wifi.BssidPreferred=<MAC>, then call method:fi.nexus.Wifi.Connect(profile_path) to roam onto it. This re-runs flow:connect-known-wifi.
Long-press alternative BSSID → 'Blacklist': append <MAC> to Profile.Wifi.BssidBlacklist, then call method:fi.nexus.Wifi.Connect to drop the current association if it matches the new blacklist.
do_not: Don't show this list when prop:fi.nexus.Wifi.State != 'connected'. The diagnostic answer it provides ('alternatives to the AP I'm on') is undefined off-network — show the full scan list instead.

Don't redo a Wifi.Scan implicitly when opening the disclosure. Honour the operator's explicit gestures; surface a 'Refresh' affordance that calls method:fi.nexus.Wifi.Scan and waits on sig:fi.nexus.Wifi.ScanComplete.
Don't compare ScanResult.Ssid by lossy UTF-8. Hidden / non-printable SSIDs collide under string equality but are distinct on the wire.

permissions_handling.title: Handling AuthFailed (polkit denial) without surprising the operator
permissions_handling.purpose: Almost every mutating method requires a polkit action. AuthFailed is policy denial, not an authentication failure of the operator's typed credentials. UIs must not conflate the two.
rules: On AuthFailed: do not retry the same call automatically. The decision was made by polkit and won't change without operator action.

If a polkit auth agent is available in the session (most desktops, Cockpit, etc.), the call will have already prompted before returning AuthFailed. Treat the AuthFailed as 'operator declined or wasn't authorized'. Render 'Sign in as administrator to <verb>' with a Retry button that re-issues the call (this re-triggers the auth agent).

If no polkit agent is available (kiosk, headless console, embedded panel without agent), surface a clear hint: 'Administrator approval required — ask the system owner.' Don't pretend a Retry will help.

Different methods need different polkit actions (fi.nexus.scan, fi.nexus.connect, fi.nexus.profile.add, fi.nexus.profile.modify, fi.nexus.set_power, …). When you serialize the verb in the prompt, take it from the method's purpose, not from the polkit action ID — operators don't read action IDs.

command_sequences._about: Scripted UI flows with the exact call/wait/render order. Every step references nodes from the graph. Use as the spec a UI implementer can follow turn-by-turn. Audience: ui builder.

wifi.scan_picker_with_connect.name: Wi-Fi: scan picker → pick → enter passphrase → connect → show result
preconditions: Bus connection open
Caller has fi.nexus.scan and fi.nexus.connect (and fi.nexus.profile.add for new networks)
subscriptions_open_first: ObjectManager InterfacesAdded/Removed at /fi/nexus1 (path-prefix filter on /fi/nexus1/interface/<ifname>/scan_result/)
PropertiesChanged on the Wi-Fi interface object (filter member=PropertiesChanged, path=<wifi-iface>)
fi.nexus.Wifi.ScanComplete on the Wi-Fi interface object
fi.nexus.Wifi.ConnectComplete on the Wi-Fi interface object
fi.nexus.Interface.StateChanged on the Wi-Fi interface object
fi.nexus.Wifi.NetworkRequest on the Wi-Fi interface object
fi.nexus.Manager.NotificationEvent at /fi/nexus1

(off-Nexus, for the connected-card IP rows) PropertiesChanged on /org/freedesktop/network1/link/_<ifindex> on org.freedesktop.network1 — open the same moment the picker opens; ifindex comes from prop:fi.nexus.Interface.Ifindex on the Wi-Fi interface.
(off-Nexus, for the DNS row) PropertiesChanged on /org/freedesktop/resolve1/link/_<ifindex> on org.freedesktop.resolve1.

steps.ui: Render 'Wi-Fi' screen header. Read Wifi.Powered; show toggle.
If Powered==false, gate the rest behind 'Turn on Wi-Fi' tap which writes Wifi.Powered=true and waits for PropertiesChanged.
Show 'Scanning…' spinner.
calls: method:fi.nexus.Wifi.Scan ({}) — empty params for default broadcast scan

errors.ResourceBusy: Show 'Driver busy, retrying' and back off >=2s before retry.
errors.RateLimited: Honour retry_after_ms; surface 'Too many scans, please wait Xs'.
errors.AuthFailed: Operator lacks fi.nexus.scan — show 'Sign in to scan' affordance.
errors.FeatureDisabled: Wi-Fi backend disabled in nexus.toml — show static 'Wi-Fi unavailable on this device'.

steps.ui: Render incoming scan_result objects as a live list. Sort by SignalDbm desc, group by SSID.
steps.wait_for: ObjectManager InterfacesAdded under <wifi-iface>/scan_result/, plus Wifi.ScanComplete to mark the list as settled.
render_per_row: ScanResult.Ssid (decode UTF-8 lossy for display, keep ay for matching)

steps.ui: User taps a row.

branches.profile_exists: Manager.FindWifiProfile(ssid:ay) — if path returned, skip to step 8 with that profile.
branches.no_profile: Continue to step 6 to collect credentials.

steps.ui: Show credential dialog matched to the SSID's security: passphrase field for WPA2/WPA3 personal; identity+password for WPA2/WPA3 Enterprise; nothing for OWE/Open.
Tap 'Save & Connect'.
calls: method:fi.nexus.Manager.AddWifiProfile (settings dict with ssid:ay, security:{type,passphrase|password|...}, auto_connect:true)

errors.AlreadyExists: Profile exists — call Manager.FindWifiProfile then Profile.Update with the new credentials. Continue to step 8.
errors.InvalidArgument: Highlight the offending field (server returns details.field hint when supported).
errors.AuthFailed: Operator lacks fi.nexus.profile.add — surface admin-auth requirement.

steps.ui: Show 'Connecting…' on the row.
wait_for_signal_sequence: Interface.StateChanged new_state=authenticating (wpa_supplicant only — skip if Wifi.Supplicant=='iwd')
Interface.StateChanged new_state=handshaking (wpa_supplicant only and security != open)

interactive_branch.ui: Render modal: 'text' as the prompt copy, secret-text input matching 'field'.
interactive_branch.reply: method:fi.nexus.Wifi.ProvideCredential(network, field, value) — pass network back verbatim
interactive_branch.post_reply: Resume waiting for the StateChanged sequence.

failure_branch.permanent_ui: Show 'Wrong password' inline; offer Profile.Update with new credential. After Update, the backend clears CredentialsInvalid and retries automatically.
failure_branch.transient_ui: Show 'Connection failed — retrying' for ~2 s while the cool-down elapses; the backend will scan and reattempt the sticky profile.

steps.ui: On Wifi.ConnectComplete success (or state=connected), render the connected card per ui_design_patterns.connected_card_recipe: SSID, signal bars (subscribe Wifi.SignalDbm hot updates), security badge, BSSID + channel (advanced disclosure, decoded from Wifi.ConnectedBss), IP / Subnet / Router / DNS rows, alternative-APs disclosure (per ui_design_patterns.alternative_aps_for_connected_ssid), Disconnect, Forget.

ip_rows._about: Nexus does NOT publish IP-layer state on fi.nexus1 (ADR-001). Read addresses, routes, and DNS from systemd-networkd / systemd-resolved on the same system bus.
calls: org.freedesktop.network1.Manager.DescribeLink(ifindex:i) on /org/freedesktop/network1 — yields a JSON blob with Addresses[] / Routes[]; extract IPv4 / IPv6 address, prefix, default gateway. (On systemd <250, fall back to the no-arg Manager.Describe() and pluck the per-link entry from JSON.Interfaces[] by Index.)
Properties.Get on /org/freedesktop/resolve1/link/_<ifindex>, interface=org.freedesktop.resolve1.Link, property=DNS — yields a(iay); decode per family for the DNS row.
rerender_triggers: PropertiesChanged on /org/freedesktop/network1/link/_<ifindex> → re-DescribeLink() and refresh IP / Subnet / Router.

post_conditions: Profile saved (auto_connect:true means it will reconnect automatically)
Connected card renders SSID/Signal/Security from fi.nexus1 plus IP/Subnet/Router/DNS from networkd+resolved

wifi.recover_credentials_invalid.name: Wi-Fi: handle a credentials-invalid notification and re-establish service
wifi.recover_credentials_invalid.trigger: Manager.NotificationEvent kind=credentials_invalid OR Profile.CredentialsInvalidChanged(true) OR Interface.StateChanged details.reason=credentials_invalid

steps.ui: Surface a banner or notification: 'Wi-Fi password rejected for <ssid>'.
User taps 'Update password'. Open passphrase entry pre-filled with the SSID label.
Submit.
Watch Profile.CredentialsInvalidChanged(false) — that's the backend confirming it has cleared the flag.
Backend will auto-retry on the next auto-connect cycle. Subscribe to Interface.StateChanged on the original interface to render reconnection.

bluetooth.pair_and_connect.name: Bluetooth: discover → pair → connect
preconditions: Adapter exists (fi.nexus.Bluetooth interface object present)
Caller has fi.nexus.connect and fi.nexus.profile.modify
subscriptions_open_first: ObjectManager InterfacesAdded/Removed at /fi/nexus1 (path-prefix filter on the adapter's /device/ subtree)
fi.nexus.Bluetooth.StateChanged on the adapter object
fi.nexus.Bluetooth.PairingStarted on the adapter object
fi.nexus.Bluetooth.PairingPrompt on the adapter object
fi.nexus.Bluetooth.PairingComplete on the adapter object
fi.nexus.BluetoothDevice.StateChanged via wildcard child path
fi.nexus.BluetoothDevice.ConnectionChanged

steps.ui: Read Bluetooth.Powered. If false, write true and wait for State=powered.
Show 'Searching for devices…'.

errors.NotPowered: Power flipped off mid-call; retry from step 1.
errors.BluezUnavailable: Show 'Bluetooth service offline' and retry on Manager.NotificationEvent kind=subsystem_recovered.

steps.ui: Render incoming device rows. Each new ObjectManager InterfacesAdded for a path under <adapter>/device/ is a row.
render_per_row: BluetoothDevice.Alias or Name (fall back to Address if both empty)

steps.ui: User taps a discovered device.
steps.capture: Returned job_id — use it to filter PairingPrompt and PairingComplete signals.

errors.InvalidState: Device may already be pairing/paired; refresh state and skip.

steps.ui: Show 'Pairing…' modal.
steps.wait_for: sig:fi.nexus.Bluetooth.PairingStarted matching job_id (confirmation that backend has begun)

steps.ui: Handle every PairingPrompt for this job_id by rendering a UI matching kind:

display_passkey.ui: Read-only screen: 'Enter <passkey> on the other device' with an Acknowledge button.

display_pin.ui: Same as display_passkey, with data.pin shown.

request_confirmation.ui: Show data.passkey and ask 'Do these match?' Yes/No.

steps.user_cancel: Any prompt may be cancelled at any time with AnswerPairingPrompt(job_id, ('s', 'cancel')) — backend treats as rejection.
steps.deadline: BlueZ Agent timeout is 60 s by default. If exceeded, PairingComplete fires with reason='timeout'.

steps.ui: Pairing terminus.

branches.success_true: Render 'Paired'. Continue to step 8 if auto-connect is desired.
branches.success_false: Render 'Pairing failed: <reason>'. reason values: rejected, timeout, auth_failed, connection_failed, other. Offer Retry (back to step 4) or Cancel.

steps.ui: Auto-Connect after pair. BluetoothDevice.State never shows a 'connecting' value — track that as UI-local state from the moment you call Connect() until one of the signals below lands.

errors.NotPaired: Should not happen post-step-7-success; treat as bug.
errors.ConnectionFailed: Show 'Couldn't connect — try again' with Retry.

steps.ui: Render the connected device card. Offer 'Disconnect' (keeps bond), 'Forget' (removes bond), 'Trust' toggle (BluetoothDevice.Trusted).
On screen exit, call StopDiscovery to release the BlueZ session (saves battery and contention with other clients).

bluetooth.reconnect_known_device.name: Bluetooth: connect to a previously-paired device (no discovery needed)
preconditions: Device exists in BluetoothDevice.KnownDevices
BluetoothDevice.Paired==true on that device

steps.ui: User taps a paired device in the list.
Show 'Connecting…' (UI-local — BluetoothDevice.State never shows a 'connecting' value).
Connected card.

errors.ConnectionFailed: Show retry. Most common cause: peer is out of range or off.

bluetooth.reconnect_known_device.ui_note: BLE devices may be unbonded but still connectable — Connect from state=discovered works for Transport=='le'. For Classic devices, NotPaired is returned and the UI must run the pair flow first.

gnss.live_position_widget.name: GNSS: render a live-position widget that survives degraded periods
preconditions: A gnss-Kind interface is registered
subscriptions_open_first: PropertiesChanged on the GNSS interface object (covers State, LastFix, SatellitesInView, SatellitesUsed, HorizontalErrorM, GpsdConnected)
fi.nexus.Gnss.FixChanged on the GNSS interface object
fi.nexus.Gnss.SatellitesChanged on the GNSS interface object
fi.nexus.Manager.NotificationEvent (for subsystem_unavailable / subsystem_recovered with subsystem='gpsd')

steps.ui: Find the GNSS interface object.
calls: ObjectManager.GetManagedObjects then filter Interface.Kind=='gnss', OR Manager.Interfaces + per-path Properties.Get Interface.Kind

steps.ui: Read snapshot.
Branch on State.

branches.pending|acquiring: Show 'Searching for satellites… <SatellitesInView> in view, <SatellitesUsed> used'. Indeterminate spinner. Update on PropertiesChanged for SatellitesInView/Used.
branches.tracking: Render position from LastFix.tuple. Show horizontal_error_m as a confidence radius on a map; satellites_used as a count.
branches.degraded: Render last-known position grayed-out, with 'Signal weak — last update Ns ago' computed from time_unix_ms in LastFix.

steps.ui: Live updates.
steps.wait_for_signal_loop: On Gnss.FixChanged, parse the (xidddddddu) tuple and re-render. Mode 0 -> hide coordinates. Mode 2 -> show lat/lon, hide altitude. Mode 3 -> show all.
steps.secondary_signal: On Gnss.SatellitesChanged, update the satellite-count chip without re-rendering the whole position widget.

steps.ui: Health watchdog.
steps.wait_for: Manager.NotificationEvent kind=subsystem_unavailable subsystem='gpsd' → show 'GPS service offline' banner. kind=subsystem_recovered subsystem='gpsd' → clear it.
steps.fallback_check: If GpsdConnected is false for >5 s, show the same banner even if no NotificationEvent has fired (covers cold-start race).

rendering_rules: Never branch UI on LastFix's zero-tuple — branch on State. The tuple is zeroed when no fix is held but is also zero at the equator/Greenwich for a short window during acquisition.
Optional fields (vertical_error_m, track_deg, altitude_m for non-3D fixes) come through as 0.0 — don't render those as 'zero', render as 'not available'.
Speed below ~0.5 m/s makes track_deg unreliable; either suppress the heading arrow or freeze it at the last known direction.

common.subscribe_before_call.name: Universal pattern — open subscriptions BEFORE issuing the triggering call
common.subscribe_before_call.rationale: Signals fire asynchronously. If you Connect() first and Subscribe() after, the first StateChanged or PairingPrompt is already on the wire and lost. Every flow above lists 'subscriptions_open_first' for this reason.
ordering: 1. Open all D-Bus subscriptions you'll need for the flow.
2. Read initial state (Properties.GetAll or ObjectManager.GetManagedObjects) to synchronize your view.
3. Issue the method call that drives the state machine.
4. React to incoming signals; never poll.
